extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR management units, facility environmental compliance staff, and state/federal regulators
extracted.subtask_short: CCR groundwater monitoring and closure requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and criteria governing groundwater monitoring, corrective action, annual reporting, closure, and post-closure care for CCR management units (CCRMU) under the CCR rule, including timelines, report contents, corrective action triggers and remedy selection, and conditions for deferral or exemption. Intended to instruct owners/operators how to document, implement, and publish compliance-related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of CCRMU must prepare an annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report no later than January 31, 2029 and annually thereafter (and earlier text: reports be due no later than January 31 of the year following the collection of the eight baseline samples and the first semi-annual sampling event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual report serves as an update on activities related to the groundwater monitoring program, including installation of monitoring wells. Timing allows facilities to provide all documentation required by §257.90(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report required contents (maps, wells, monitoring data, narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must document activities associated with the groundwater monitoring program and progress of corrective action and must contain specific information identified in the regulations, including but not limited to maps; aerial images or diagrams showing the CCRMU and all upgradient (background) and downgradient wells; identification of any monitoring wells installed or decommissioned in the previous year; monitoring data collected under §§257.90 through 257.98; and a narrative discussion of any transition between monitoring programs (i.e., detection and assessment monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporting requirement helps ensure groundwater level data collected over the period is tabulated, presented, and analyzed to determine groundwater levels relative to any residual CCR left in place and to confirm or determine groundwater flow directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate well locations and depths annually
rubrics_metrics.description: Upgradient and downgradient well locations and depths should be validated annually with respect to measured and mapped flow directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation ensures accurate interpretation of monitoring results relative to groundwater flow and supports identification of background vs downgradient conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include and summarize groundwater quality sampling data; tabulate exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater quality sampling data should be included in appendices and summarized and tabulated in the annual reports. If appropriate, exceedances (SSIs and SSLs) of Appendix III and IV constituents should be tabulated and highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports should identify the nearest downgradient surface water bodies as well as groundwater supply wells in the vicinity of the unit to contextualize exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting basic data and QA/QC in annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual corrective action and monitoring reports must contain the basic data which informs positions and status reported in those documents, including but not limited to boring logs, monitoring well installation diagrams, water level data, field sampling data sheets for groundwater sample collection, laboratory analytical data including QA/QC data, data validation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be organized so (1) compliance with the CCR regulations is evident; (2) data supporting compliance conclusions are easily located within the document; and (3) the public is readily able to review the groundwater monitoring data and related information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post annual report on public CCR website and make it accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator must not only document compliance in the annual report, but also post the annual report on the public CCR website to allow the public to review the groundwater monitoring results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name of the document on the public CCR website should be such that it is clear what the file is and it must be capable of being readily printed and downloaded by the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply existing corrective action requirements (§§257.96-257.98) to CCRMU
rubrics_metrics.description: If groundwater monitoring demonstrates an exceedance of the groundwater protection standards for constituents identified in Appendix IV of part 257, corrective action is required, as laid out in §§257.96 through 257.98. These requirements apply throughout the active life and any post-closure care period of the CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is finalizing that CCRMU comply with existing corrective action requirements; these requirements include initiating ACMs, selecting remedies that attain groundwater protection standards, and implementing remedial activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action timing: ACM initiation/completion, remedy selection/implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: §257.96(a) requires an ACM be initiated within 90 days of determining an SSL has occurred and then completed within another 90 days. An extension, not to exceed 60 days, may be warranted due to site-specific conditions or circumstances. Once the ACM is complete, a remedy must be selected as soon as feasible. The corrective action program requires the owner/operator to initiate remedial activities within 90 days of selecting a remedy (§257.98(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected remedy must meet prescribed standards, including attaining groundwater protection standards. Implementation of source control (e.g., removal) does not negate the requirement to implement the groundwater remediation portion within a reasonable time in accordance with the schedule in the remedy selection report. EPA expects assessors to consider impacts on the nearest surface water bodies and nearest private/public groundwater wells when selecting remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct simultaneous sampling to expedite detection and corrective action (proposed rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting the sampling simultaneously would expedite groundwater monitoring and, where necessary, initiation of corrective action by at least six months at sites where units have potentially been leaking for a long period of time. Expediting Appendix IV constituent detection, assessment and any required corrective action would protect human health and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was proposed as a means to accelerate detection and action; the preamble explains the public-health rationale for quicker simultaneous sampling at historically leaking sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply closure and post-closure requirements (§§257.101-257.104) to CCRMU (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires CCRMU that contain 1,000 tons or greater of CCR to comply with the existing closure and post-closure care requirements in §§257.101 through 257.104, except for the alternative closure requirements in §257.103(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA extended the existing dewatering requirement in §257.102(d)(2)(i) to any CCR landfill constructed in groundwater or otherwise saturated by liquids, and incorporated a definition of 'infiltration' in §257.53. Closure is deemed the effective, uniform preventive method to address potential or existing releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for mandatory closure (1,000 tons)
rubrics_metrics.description: CCR management units containing 1,000 tons or greater of CCR are required to close under the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reasoned this threshold provides significant risk mitigation and is consistent with protecting human health and the environment; closure addresses source control and prevention of future contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral for CCRMU closed under prior alternative requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is deferring, in certain cases, the requirement to demonstrate compliance with §257.102 for CCRMU that closed prior to the effective date of this rule in accordance with alternative requirements that are likely to be as protective as the requirements in §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision aligns with the approach for legacy CCR surface impoundments and avoids unnecessary rework where prior closures are likely as protective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral to initiate closure for CCRMU under critical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is deferring the requirement to initiate closure where the CCRMU is located beneath critical infrastructure or large buildings or structures vital to the continuation of current site activities (e.g., high power electric transmission towers, air pollution control or wastewater treatment systems, large buildings, or an electrical substation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral lasts until the infrastructure is no longer needed, a permit authority determines closure is necessary to ensure no reasonable probability of adverse effects on human health or the environment, or the closure or decommissioning of the facility—whichever occurs first. EPA cited concerns about potential adverse localized impacts on electric reliability and lack of record to determine impacts are unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended deadline to initiate closure (allow groundwater data to inform closure)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has extended the deadline to initiate closure to Wednesday, November 8, 2028 (48 months from the effective date of the final rule) to allow groundwater monitoring data to inform closure decisions, consistent with the approach for legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extension responds to comments about feasibility, seasonality, overlapping regulatory requirements, and resource constraints and allows completion of monitoring systems and baseline sampling before closure actions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate previously closed CCRMU for compliance with §257.102(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not requiring previously closed CCRMU to automatically re-close but requires owners/operators to evaluate whether the unit meets the requirements of §257.102(d), and if they do not, to take such measures as are necessary to bring the unit into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires a review of prior closures and corrective action where necessary if the unit does not meet current requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure justified as preventive, not solely remedial
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure requirements are intended to prevent contamination from occurring in the first place by ensuring that the closed unit does not become a source of future contamination; corrective actions are remedial for contamination that has already occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA contrasts closure under subtitles C and D with corrective-action-only approaches and finds closure warranted for CCRMU because regulatory history and risk assessments demonstrate substantial present and potential future risks even where contamination is not yet detected above GWPS.
